newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Kapuas plans stock split, expansion.
newsitem.headline: Kapuas plans stock split, expansion.

text.p: Indonesian glue manufacturer PT Kurnia Kapuas Utama Glue Industries said on Wednesday it planned a stock split and to expand its activities into other sectors.
Kurnia Kapuas rose 16.67 percent, or 400 rupiah, to 2,800 rupiah in active late trading on Wednesday.
"We have a plan for a stock split as well as to expand our business outside of glue, but the plans are still in their infancy," corporate secretary Jeffery Goh told Reuters.
Goh said the firm had submitted the plan to the stock market authorities on Wednesday and the firm expected to obtain shareholder approval at a meeting on February 28.
Kapuas planned a two-for-one split, taking its nominal share price to 500 rupiah from 1,000 rupiah per share, to boost the firm's liquidity on the stockmarket, Goh said.
He declined to give details on the firm's expansion plans, only saying it could be upstream or downstream, but not too far from its current core business.
Goh confirmed market talk that the firm was expected to post strong net profit in 1996, but declined to give any figures.
Kapuas posted a net profit of 9.1 billion rupiah in 1995 against 5.8 billion rupiah in 1994.
